caption: Table 68-10. General therapy for patients with hepatobiliary disease.*
rows: Use potassium-replete food or potassium supplement
Avoid alkalosis in patients with hepatic encephalopathy
Add dextrose to parenteral fluids as needed
Ensure that daily energy requirement is being met; if not, begin assisted feeding
Add B vitamins to fluids or give as injection
Modify feeding plan to control complications
Modify food and prevent formation and absorption of enteric toxins
Use retention enemas q6h containing lactulose or povidone iodine solution
Treat GI parasites, treat gastric ulcers, avoid drugs that exacerbate GI hemorrhage (e.g., aspirin, glucocorticoids)
Avoid drugs or therapies that exacerbate hepatic encephalopathy
Do not administer sedatives, analgesics, anesthetics, diuretics, stored blood or methionine-containing products
Use appropriate anticonvulsant drugs (e.g., potassium bromide)
Give fresh plasma or blood transfusion as needed
Give H2 blockers (e.g., ranitidine) or cytoprotective agents (e.g., sucralfate)
Give systemic antibiotics (e.g., penicillin, ampicillin, cephalosporins, aminoglycosides, metronidazole)
Give bile “altering” or choleretic drugs (e.g., ursodiol)
note: 原表无表头行（左列为治疗目标/类别，右列为具体措施），故列名为空字符串；加粗类别行单独成行、右列为空。
